Game Tools
Farm
Needs You
Things Claude made that wait on you: placeholder art to swap for your own, numbers only you can pick, sounds to put on the SD card, things to try on the board. Open a file in its editor, tick it when it's yours, and write any answer in the box — it's saved in assets/needs_you.json, and Claude reads it there next time.
Fishing
Stardew Valley style fishing. Everything here is an item in assets/items/: fish (caught with a rod, after a fight), junk (fished up instead now and then), crab pot catches (a crab pot in the water catches one overnight), treasure (found in the chests that sink into the fight), bait and tackle (put on a rod by dropping them on it in the bag), and rods. Pick one on the left (or make a new one), give it its icon, say where and when it shows up, and Save — then rebuild the firmware. Map water is a pond unless its asset says River or Ocean (the Map Editor: select a Fishable asset → Water:).
Who bites? — try a spot
What the game would pick right now at a place like this, with this gear (the same sums as the firmware). Change anything and it works it out again.
Game-wide settings (assets/fishing/settings.c)
Furniture
Furniture you want in the game, and what each piece should do — a TV that shows channels, a lamp that lights the room at night, a chair to sit on. Fill it in and press Add to the list. It's saved in assets/furniture.json (pictures in assets/furniture/); tell Claude "build the furniture list" and it makes each one an item, gives it its function and marks it built here. Furniture that's already in the game is at the bottom: give any of it a new function the same way.

The list
Already in the game
Every item in assets/items/ ticked "Can be placed" (beds, aquariums, shelves, rugs, farm props…), with what it does now. Give it a new function… puts a change to it on the list above for Claude; Open in Item Editor changes its art, price or settings yourself.
Wardrobe genders
Who wears each piece: male, neutral or female. Each shopper in the game is a man or a woman and only wears their own pieces and the neutral ones; your own character can wear anything, and Customize's lists go male first, neutral in the middle, female last. Click a button (or press M N F, or 1 2 3) and the next piece comes up; Backspace goes back, Space skips. Saved in assets/wardrobe/genders.json as you go — the board picks it up at the next build. Untagged pieces count as neutral.

Crops Editor
Crop
Only the bottom 16×16 (the planted tile) ever blocks. The top half never does. The player is always drawn under the crop.
Prices & rarity
What the player gets for selling one. 0 = can't be sold.
What a shop charges for one packet. 0 = no shop sells it.
Grows in
Seasons are 28 game days each. In game it can only be planted in these, the seed shop only sells the packet then, and it withers on the first day of a season it doesn't grow in. Inside buildings (a greenhouse) it grows any time. None ticked = all year.
☆Standard ×1 ★Silver 20% ×1.25 ★Gold 6% ×1.5 ★Emerald 1.5% ×2
The same rarity works for any item: tick "Rolls a quality" in the Item Editor.

Buildings Editor
Building
The footprint is the bottom rows of tiles: they're solid and stand on Buildable ground. The rows above are the roof — the player walks behind them. The door is one tile of the footprint's bottom row; walking into it goes inside. Click the picture: on the bottom row to move the door, higher up to set where the footprint starts.
The map exported for its inside, without .map (blank = no way in). Give that map a teleporter with "Building exit" ticked, by its door: it's where the player walks in, and how they get back out. Every building put up gets its own copy of the inside.
Item that places it
Its item has the same id and name. Held in game, a hologram of the building shows in front of the player; tapping the hologram builds it there.

Seasonal art
Seasons are 28 game days each. In a season this asset has art for, every copy of it on the map is drawn with that art instead; the others use the normal art. Collision, layers and actions stay the same, and the seasonal art can't paint past the normal art's shape (see-through there = what's under it shows). Click Load PNG…, drop a PNG on a season, or try Auto for a first draft. Export the map again afterwards.

Shop Editor
Put any item up for sale: tick it, give it a price and pick a counter. "Usual" sends it where it belongs (props → Build, seeds and farm tools → Seeds, animal things → Ranch, rods, bait, tackle and crab pots → Fish, anything else → General store). In game every shop has a tab for each counter with stock; put a shop on a map with an asset action (Map Editor › Actions…: Seed / Build / Ranch / Fish shop, General store). Seeds, animals, buildings and machines keep their price in their own editors.

Into a new folder
Adjust this frame, then Apply — a new library asset is created with the result; the original is left unchanged.
Shift nudges the art by pixels (a breathing bob, a swing offset). Tilt rotates it — pivot at the bottom for a sway (grass, a hit tree) or the centre for a spin (a coin, a projectile). Squash/stretch scales width/height independently, anchored at the bottom, for landing/impact bounces. Flash blends toward white — handy for a hit-flash frame on a breakable. Collision and layer move with the art.
Placing this asset plays an animation over its footprint: cut this asset's own PNG into frames (sprite sheet), or pick a shared Frame Bundle whose size matches this asset's own W×H, or create one without leaving this dialog. Collision and layer come from this asset's own pixels (paint them with Modify) — the bundle only supplies the frames that play back on top.
Sprite sheet — animate this asset's own PNG: it's cut into equal frames, the asset becomes frame 1 and places at that size.
— or play a Frame Bundle from the library —
Level 0 is this asset itself, exactly as it looks in the library (its own pixels/collision/layer — paint them with Modify). Add more levels for what it breaks into next, each with its own idle look and a Frame Bundle for the hit effect; each can be smaller than this asset (a tree leaving a log) and sits inside its footprint, bottom-centre unless you move it. Every level's hit-effect bundle is the same size as that level's own image. "Needs item" is what the player must be holding to hit it — any item can act as a tool.
Sound Bundles
A sound bundle is a name for a list of sounds that play one after another. Type the bundle's name in a breakable's Hit sound or Break sound box, the same way you'd type one sound. Sounds are .wav files in D:\CaptureIt\sounds\sound effects on the S3's SD card. Type them without ".wav" and separate them with commas. The S3 plays 16-bit mono WAVs at 44100 Hz, up to 8 sounds in one list. Export the map again after changing a bundle.
Folder
Item Editor
Item
Selling & dropping
In game: pick the stack up in the inventory and drop it on SELL.
DROP in the inventory puts the stack on the map as a 16×16 tile; walking onto it picks it back up.
Each time the player gets one (a breakable drops it) it can come out Silver ★ (20%, ×1.25 price), Gold ★ (6%, ×1.5) or Emerald ★ (1.5%, ×2); otherwise Standard, no star.
Every item the player catches, harvests or gets from a breakable can come out mutated — it looks different everywhere (bag, ground, in their hands, animated while held), sells for more and doesn't stack with plain ones. Heavy squashes the player while they hold it; Floaty floats up and down above their head. The multiplier boosts the rarer mutations the most; ×0 = never (e.g. for tools or building materials). Shops never sell mutated things.
Farming tools
Animal things (Animals Editor): hay feeds a hungry animal, a scythe cuts grass (half the time into hay), grass starter plants grass on Tillable ground (it spreads; animals eat it), shears and the milk pail take an animal's product. With a price they're sold in the Ranch shop.
Hoe: held in game, tap ground ticked "Tillable" in the Map Editor to turn it into farmland. Watering can: tap farmland, or a crop growing in it, to water it for the day — each tile uses one of the water it holds; tap a well or water to fill it again (0 = it never runs dry). Crops only grow on days their soil was watered (rain waters it too); it all dries out overnight. A tool with a price ("Sold in shops", below) is sold in the Seed shop.
Placing (furniture)
A shelf, a crate, a rug… Held in game, a hologram of it shows in front of the player (green = fits, red = doesn't); tap the hologram to put it down, tap it with empty hands to pick it up. What's placed is the first frame of its held art — at most 64×64 px, standing on a footprint as many tiles wide as the art.
Footprint rows: how many tile rows at the bottom stand on the floor (0 = all of it). The rows above hang over and are drawn in front of the player, like a tall lamp. Untick Solid for something walked on, like a rug.
In game, tapping a placed shelf opens it: put things from the bag on it, set each one's price, and customers come in and make offers on them (you accept or decline), even while you're on another map — the further over what it's worth, the fewer offers. What's on it shows on it, side by side, standing on the row (0 = half way down; click the preview to set it). Picking a shelf up needs it empty.
Tapping a placed bed asks "Go to bed?": SLEEP skips to 6:00 the next morning, and crops in watered soil grow overnight. PICK UP takes it back. With a sheet layer it's walked into like in Stardew: the player gets in from the left or right side, the sheet covers them, and lying there asks. Only the frame blocks: the headboard rows above the first number and the footboard rows from the second (0 = the usual: 22 and 16 px up from the bottom). The player lies on the footprint's second-to-last tile row, so the gap must hold those rows. (A bed drawn into a map instead gets the "Bed" action in the Map Editor's Actions….)
Tapping a placed aquarium while holding a fish puts the fish in, and it swims around the tank (only on the map the player is on). With empty hands it takes the last fish out, and picks the tank up once it's empty. The fish keep inside the box set by the attributes aqua_x, aqua_y, aqua_w, aqua_h (px from the art's top-left; none = 3 px in from each side).
3×3
Every morning at 6:00 a placed sprinkler waters the farmland in the square around it — 1 = 3×3 (Bronze), 2 = 5×5 (Silver), 3 = 7×7 (Gold), 4 = 9×9 (Emerald) — and sprays until 7:00. A crop picked less than an hour after its farmland was watered comes out Wet. Holding one in game shows its square. (Props can't stand on farmland: leave its tile untilled.)
15×15
Every morning each crop has a 4% chance of being eaten by a crow (it waits where the crop was, then caws and flies off when you come near) — unless it's inside a placed scarecrow's square: 7 = 15×15.
Any item with a price is for sale. "Usual" puts it where it belongs: props in the Build shop, a hoe or watering can in the Seed shop, animal things at the Ranch, rods / bait / tackle / crab pots in the Fish shop, anything else in the General store — or pick a counter. Each shop is an asset action in the Map Editor; every shop has a tab for each counter with stock. The Shop Editor tab sets this for many items at once.
Crafting
In game: the hammer tab on top of the inventory shows every item with a recipe, like Stardew's crafting page — faded until the bag holds the ingredients. Tap one to see what it takes, tap it again to craft one. The ingredients come out of the bag (the plainest stacks first) and the item goes in at normal quality. Ingredients are item ids (the Item list below).
Fishing
Held in game, tap water (ground ticked "Fishable" in the Map Editor) to cast. In the minigame, hold the screen to lift the green catch bar, let go and it sinks — keep the fish inside it until the meter fills.
Rod stats
The tick mark on each slider is a normal rod. A good rod can be worse at something else. Hover a name for what it does.
Catch bar
Reel speed
Bite speed
Luck
Grip
Any rod can catch it on Fishable water between those hours (to lower than from = overnight, e.g. 20 to 4) in that weather. Rarity is how often it bites against the other fish that could (10 = normal, 1 = rare). Difficulty 1-100 is how wildly it swims in the minigame; "Swims": darting = sudden jumps, smooth = slow glides, sinker / floater = keeps to the bottom / top. Tick "Rolls a quality" for Silver / Gold / Emerald catches — a perfect catch (it never left the bar) is one better.

Tag as a fish
How rare is it? The tier sets how often it bites against the other fish that could (its Rarity, which you can still fine-tune on the card) and shows in game: Rare and up colour the bite "!" and the fish in the minigame, and the catch card names it.
Mutation multiplier
How much more likely this fish is to come out mutated. It boosts the rare mutations the most, so a big multiplier makes a Rainbow or Celestial catch a real possibility. On top of it: a perfect catch ×2, rain ×1.25, a lucky rod up to ×2.
Teleporter
Invisible in the game. When the player walks onto it, the device loads the map below and stands the player on the arrival tile. Leave the map blank to jump somewhere on this same map. Positions are 16 px tiles — the chip under the map shows the tile under the cursor, and View ▸ Show grid + coords numbers every tile (open the arrival map in a tab to read its numbers).
The name you exported that map as, without .map — "cave" loads CaptureIt/maps/cave/cave.map on the SD card.
For a building's inside (the map a Buildings Editor building leads into): walking onto it goes back out, to the door of whichever building the player came in by. The player also arrives standing on it when they walk in, so put it by the inside's door, on the bottom edge.

Actions
When the player taps a placed copy of this asset in the game, they walk up to it and the ticked actions run, in the order you ticked them. The list comes from main/actions.c (every ASSET_ACTION row): add a function there, rebuild the firmware, then Reload here. Export the map again after changing these.
Frame Bundle Library
A bundle is a strip of frames plus how long each stays up and how many times to loop. Save one here, then point any Map Animation placement or Breakable hit effect at it by name — the same bundle can be reused everywhere its frame size (W×H) fits, so it's only ever stored once.
Existing bundles
New bundle
✨ Premade effect — made from any art, at that art's own size. It fills in the frames below; Save it like any bundle.
Leave out — click 16×16 squares of the art to drop them from every frame: they just disappear (e.g. a tree's trunk base, so the stump left behind shows instead of a second one falling). Click again to put one back; drag to do several.
Frames — build the bundle one frame at a time. Duplicate copies the last frame in so you can tweak it with Modify instead of starting over; Modify edits a frame's own pixels on the main canvas, exactly like an asset's Modify.
— or —
Shortcut: import a sprite-sheet strip and auto-slice it into frames
